title: The Quarreling Quails
text:
The Jataka tells that the future Buddha was once born as a quail and led a large flock in the forest. A fowler had learned to imitate the call of quails. When the birds gathered at his call, he threw his net over them, stuffed them in his basket, and sold them.

The leader of the flock taught the others a defense. When the net fell, each quail should push its head through a mesh, and then all should fly up together, carrying the net, and drop it on a thornbush. They could then slip out underneath. It worked. Day after day the fowler threw his net and watched it fly away, and he came home empty-handed and had to free it from the thorns.

Then one day, as the quails landed to feed, one bird accidentally stepped on another's head. The second bird snapped at him, and soon they were arguing over who lifted the net and who did not. The leader saw what this meant and took the wise birds away with him to another place. The next time the fowler cast his net, the quarreling quails each waited for the others to lift it. He gathered them all up and carried them off.
lesson: A team's best method only works while its members still trust one another. Quarrels about who does the most can destroy the cooperation that keeps everyone safe.
people: The Bodhisatta as a quail, the quail flock, a fowler
